subject: physics
topicDisplay: Theme B · Thermal Energy Transfers & Greenhouse Effect
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Temperature is a measure of the:
options: Average kinetic energy of the particles
questions.explain: Internal energy is the total; temperature reflects average random kinetic energy.

questions.q: Thermal energy spontaneously flows from:
questions.explain: Heat flows down a temperature gradient to thermal equilibrium.

questions.q: The heat to change temperature (no state change) is:
questions.explain: Mass x specific heat capacity x temperature change.

questions.q: Heating 2.0 kg of water (c = 4180 J/kg/K) by 10 K requires:
The energy for a change of state at constant temperature is the:
questions.explain: Q = mL; particle potential energy changes at constant temperature.

questions.q: During melting the temperature stays constant because energy supplied:
options: Breaks forces between particles rather than raising kinetic energy
questions.explain: Latent heat increases potential energy, not temperature, during the change.

questions.q: Heat transfer through a solid metal is mainly by:
questions.explain: Conduction transfers energy via particle collisions and free electrons.

questions.q: Convection transfers energy by:
options: Bulk movement of a heated fluid
questions.explain: Warm fluid rises and cool fluid sinks, forming convection currents.

questions.q: Thermal radiation:
options: Travels through a vacuum as electromagnetic waves
questions.explain: Infrared radiation needs no medium (e.g. from the Sun).

questions.q: A perfect black body:
options: Absorbs and emits all radiation incident on it
questions.explain: An ideal absorber and emitter at all wavelengths.

questions.q: As an object gets hotter, its peak emitted wavelength (Wien's law):
questions.explain: Hotter bodies peak at shorter wavelengths (red to white heat).

questions.q: Two objects are in thermal equilibrium when:
options: They are at the same temperature with no net heat flow
questions.explain: Equal temperatures give no net thermal transfer.

questions.q: The greenhouse effect warms Earth because greenhouse gases:
options: Absorb and re-emit outgoing infrared radiation
questions.explain: They trap re-radiated infrared, warming the lower atmosphere.

questions.q: Which is a significant greenhouse gas?
questions.explain: CO2, water vapour and methane are greenhouse gases; N2 and O2 are not.

questions.q: Earth re-radiates absorbed solar energy mainly as:
questions.explain: The cooler Earth radiates in the infrared, which greenhouse gases absorb.

questions.q: The enhanced greenhouse effect from human emissions leads to:
questions.explain: More greenhouse gas increases infrared trapping, warming the planet.

questions.q: Water is a good engine coolant partly because it has a:
questions.explain: It absorbs much heat with a modest temperature rise.

questions.q: 5000 J melts ice at 0 degrees C (L = 334000 J/kg). The mass melted is about:
Evaporation cools the remaining liquid because:
options: The most energetic molecules escape, lowering the average energy
questions.explain: Losing high-energy molecules reduces average kinetic energy and temperature.

questions.q: Internal energy is the total of the particles':
questions.explain: It sums random kinetic and intermolecular potential energies.
